transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Mostly I came in because I’ve just been tired in a way that doesn’t really make sense. I can sleep, and I’m still keeping up at work, but I feel like I’m running on a low battery before the day even really gets going.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not like I’m crying all the time or anything, but for a long time now most days have this gray, flat feeling to them. Stuff I used to look forward to—like going fishing, working on the tomatoes, or a church concert—just feels more like something to get through, like it’s on a checklist instead of something I’m actually enjoying.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah. I can usually fall asleep okay, but I wake up around four in the morning and my head’s already going—server problems, compliance deadlines, things like that. Then I just lie there until the alarm, and it feels like the sleep didn’t really do much.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get worn down and discouraged, but I haven’t been thinking about hurting myself.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?
I’m not sure I’d say a lot. I mean, I think about things that need doing, but I haven’t really noticed myself worrying when there’s nothing going on.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?

Yeah, a bit. My appetite’s been off more days than not. I’ll work through lunch and not even notice, then at dinner I just kind of pick at my food. My wife mentioned my pants are fitting looser, and I’m not trying to lose weight.
Have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty lately?
I don’t think so. I get frustrated with myself sometimes, sure, but I wouldn’t say I feel worthless or overly guilty.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
Not really. I mean, I can get distracted like anyone, but I haven’t noticed any real trouble concentrating.
Have you been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself moving slower or talking slower than usual.
How long have you been feeling this gray, flat mood most days?
It’s been about two years and four months now. It started around when I got pulled back into full operational leadership, and it’s just kind of stayed there most days.
During those two years and four months, have there been any stretches as long as two months when your mood felt back to normal?
No, I don’t think there’s been a stretch that long. It’s pretty much been there most days since I got pulled back into that operational leadership role, about two years and four months ago.
Along with the low mood, have you been feeling low on energy or easily fatigued most days?

Yes. That’s actually one of the main reasons I came in. I feel tired in a way that doesn’t really add up. I can sleep, and I’m still keeping up at work, but I feel like I’m running on a low battery before the day even really starts.
Have you been feeling badly about yourself?
I’m not sure I’d say that. I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed a steady feeling of being bad about myself.
Have you been feeling unusually sensitive to cold lately?
No, I haven’t really noticed being unusually sensitive to cold. Nothing that stands out to me.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized or upbeat for several days in a row?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t really remember a stretch where I felt unusually energized or upbeat like that for several days.
Has anyone else told you that you seem slowed down lately?
No, no one’s mentioned that to me. I haven’t really noticed myself moving or talking slower either.
Have you been feeling hopeless lately?

Yeah… somewhat. I don’t know if I’d call it completely hopeless, but most days have felt pretty gray and flat for a long time. Even things I used to look forward to—like fishing, working on the tomatoes, or going to a church concert—just feel like things I’m checking off a list now, not really enjoying.
Do you often feel like you’re not good enough?
I don’t know… not often, I guess. I have days where I’m harder on myself than I should be, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly thinking I’m not good enough.
During this time, has there ever been a two-week period when your depression felt clearly worse than your usual baseline?

I don’t know that there’s been a clear two-week stretch where it was suddenly much worse. It’s more that, for a long time, most days have had this gray, flat feeling. Even things I used to look forward to—fishing, tending the tomatoes, going to a church concert—just feel like things I’m getting through rather than really enjoying.
Do you often have low self-esteem?
Not especially. I mean, I can get down on myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I often feel like I have low self-esteem.
